question:
A 37-year-old male patient comes to the office reporting left-sided rib pain for the past two weeks,
which intensifies with deep breathing and coughing. He reports no history of trauma and denies use of
tobacco or alcohol. Physical assessment reveals normal cardiac and pulmonary findings, but identifies
an exhalation dysfunction affecting the 9th through 11th ribs on the left side. The patient is positioned
for direct muscle energy treatment to address the rib dysfunction. What is the most appropriate
instruction to give the patient during the active phase of this treatment? Answer Choices: (A) rotate his
torso to the left against resistance (B) extend his left arm against resistance (C) lift his left hip toward
his left shoulder (D) depress his left ribcage during exhalation (E) push his left elbow toward the right
anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) (F) flex his left arm against resistance (G) push his left shoulder
posteriorly against the table (H) pull his left arm inferiorly against resistance (I) contract his left oblique
muscles by side-bending to the left (J) adduct his abducted left arm
 A. lift his left hip toward his left shoulder

B. push his left elbow toward the right anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)
C. pull his left arm inferiorly against resistance
D. depress his left ribcage during exhalation
E. adduct his abducted left arm
F. contract his left oblique muscles by side-bending to the left
G. extend his left arm against resistance
H. flex his left arm against resistance
I. push his left shoulder posteriorly against the table
J. rotate his torso to the left against resistance
